name: MOOGM Euljiro
detail: The bus stop and subway are very close, safe even in the early morning or at night, allowing you to go anywhere. With excellent access, I would quickly return to drop off my shopping when my bags got heavy. There is also a convenience store nearby. (From Gimpo Airport, you can get there directly by subway without any transfers. There is a limousine bus stop next to the subway station for Incheon Airport.) There are many markets and restaurants within walking distance, and the river flowing in front of the hotel has clean water, making it pleasant to walk to Dongdaemun. The room and facilities were simple, clean, stylish, and comfortable. There is a powerful hairdryer, a curling iron, and amenities like shampoo, body soap, toothbrushes, and earplugs are provided. (I found it convenient to bring disposable slippers for indoor use, the shower room, and the toilet.) The check-in and check-out system was easy and quick, saving time. I stayed alone for three nights, and it was sufficient just for sleeping. I would like to use this hotel again when I come to Korea alone.

name: Hotelette Seoul station
detail: I chose this budget hotel near Seoul Station because it was good. The facilities are commensurate with the price, but they provided the bare essentials like towels, a hairdryer, and water. I was puzzled that the toilet, sink, and shower were in the same space, but hot water came out smoothly, and it was clean, so I had no issues. The room itself is small, but the bed is comfortable to sleep on, and overall, I am satisfied.

name: PATIO7 Hotel
detail: I stayed with my high school daughter in February. - We arrived at 2 AM, but there was staff at the reception and we were able to check in. - Check-out was at 12 PM, so we could play around before leaving. - During our 3-night stay, we received pet water every day, and they made the beds for us. - I requested side-by-side beds in advance, and we got a room with side-by-side beds. - The bathroom had a washlet toilet, and it was the type where you could flush paper. - The bath had a bathtub. The bathrobe was made of soft cotton material and was comfortable to wear. - We could connect to Netflix and YouTube. - There was a bus stop a minute's walk from the hotel, and we could take the bus to places like Sinsa and Apgujeong. - Next to the hotel, there was an A Twosome Coffee cafe, and we received a half-price coupon for Americano, which we used.

name: Hanok Hotel Daam
detail: I stayed in a dormitory for 3 nights. Although it's called a dormitory, it's not a bunk bed setup, so the ceiling is high, allowing for changing clothes while standing. The location is excellent. The National Palace and Insadong are within walking distance, and both Anguk Station and Jongno Samga Station are accessible. There are plenty of convenience stores and restaurants in the area. I was also satisfied with the breakfast, which included a daily soup, salad, bread, fried rice, eggs, sautéed vegetables, and fruit. There are several staff members who speak fluent Japanese. The only downside is that there seemed to be a lack of washrooms (including handwashing facilities in the toilet) compared to the overall facilities. The facility itself was very clean, and overall I was satisfied.

name: Hotel Peyto Samseong
detail: The front staff processed everything concisely with simple English communication. It was a pleasant experience. The hotel is close to Line 2, so it was not difficult to walk with a suitcase. I also used Line 9 to go to the KSPO concert, and it was easy to walk to the station. There is a casino building along the way, and there seemed to be security, which was reassuring. I don't think there is a problem with safety. There are restaurants, convenience stores, a department store, McDonald's, and COEX nearby, so I had no trouble with shopping or dining. The convenience store on the first floor of the hotel is small, so I bought drinks and snacks there, but for meals, the convenience store a bit further away had a better selection. The room was kept clean, and the towel exchange, water replenishment, and garbage collection were all done meticulously, making my stay comfortable every day. The room size is small, but it was sufficient for my solo trip. I could open my suitcase, and there was a table and chair, so I didn't encounter any issues. The only thing that was a bit concerning was the orientation of the room; I could hear the sound of people dragging their suitcases on the road from early morning (around 3 am), which woke me up several times. Overall, I had a very comfortable stay, so considering the location and price, I would like to use this place again.

name: HOTEL DRIP&DROP Myeongdong Central
detail: We love our room! Very nice and clean. Across the street from myeongdong walking street and a few minutes walk to myeongdong station. Same with Airport us, just accross the street! Will definitely book again when we come back!

name: Nouvelle Seoul Hotel Itaewon by Anook
detail: It was convenient as it was close to the station. The downside is that there is a very steep hill to climb, so it's better to avoid going there with heavy luggage or wearing heels. The room was clean, and the Wifi was comfortable. The towels and linens were not changed daily, but they were available upon request. It was nice to have free mineral water in both the lobby and the room. There was no microwave in the room. There was a stylish speaker. Since it was a business trip, it would have been better if the desk for working was more equipped. It was nice to have Korean cuisine for breakfast.

name: Hotel MyeongDong Station
detail: It is right next to Myeongdong Station, and the location is undeniably excellent. The room is a studio type and not very spacious, but it's enough for just sleeping. The floors are separated for men on the first floor and women on the second, which provides peace of mind. Due to the thin walls, the sounds from the front desk bell and footsteps in the hallway echo a bit, but the shared facilities were outstanding. The toilet and shower are shared but new and very clean. The toilet has a washlet, and it's a kind that's rare in Korea because you can flush toilet paper directly. I was also pleased to find a Dyson hairdryer. Breakfast was plentifully provided in the refrigerator, and I could freely make coffee, fruit, instant noodles, etc. The reception responds via iPad chat when you ring the bell, and they can communicate in Japanese, making it smooth. Location, price, and shared facilities get an excellent rating, while the room gets a good rating. Overall, it was a very satisfying stay!

name: SL Hotel Myeongdong
detail: It was nice that it was located just a little away from the bustling area of Myeongdong. It was very convenient. The elevator was unusually slow, and depending on the room, the shower was lukewarm and wouldn't get hot, which was disappointing. The room temperature was just right, and I slept well! The staff included someone who spoke Japanese, which was helpful, and I was happy to receive a free room upgrade. I would like to come again.

name: Dormy Inn EXPRESS SEOUL Insadong
detail: I like Dormy Inn, so I tend to go when I'm in Japan as well. The Insadong location's sauna and breakfast area were smaller than the Gangnam location, but it was tidy, and the room size was actually larger, which was nice. The ice cream and late-night soba weren't of high quality, but I enjoyed them because they were free! Unlike the Gangnam location, there was a boiled egg with the soba^^. Located between Insadong and Ikseon-dong, there were many foreign guests, but everyone seemed quiet and went out sightseeing, so the breakfast area, which I expected to be busy, was actually quite peaceful, which was nice. Overall, it was quiet, clean, and good for hanging out in the surrounding area.
